hook.headline: 81% of Global CIOs Say They Have Lost Oversight of Their Own AI Agents

platform_cuts.linkedin:
A new Dataiku/Harris Poll survey of 685 CIOs says 81% lack complete oversight of agents created outside approved systems or formal channels. Nearly three in four (72%) can’t consistently confirm whether their agents are delivering the outcomes they were built for.

I think agents are both overhyped and genuinely promising. The conversation is confused because there’s no objective definition of an agent. Anything that doesn’t require continuous prompting is getting labeled as one. There’s cachet in deploying agents and talking about it publicly.

You paint yourself as further ahead than everyone else, and widespread AI anxiety fuels demand for that signal. But if you can’t see the agents or measure what they do, what are you actually managing?

The organizations figuring this out have an AI lead who is AI-native, or close to it, overseeing usage across the company. When AI lives inside the legacy IT department, you get process and compliance. Experimentation and cost discipline come from giving it its own home.
